cat > /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-guillaumeloulier-PhpstormProjects-oss-elephc--claude-worktrees-streams-csv-signature/c8dbe38f-1f79-484f-9b83-62bacab9ca56/scratchpad/uv/msg31.txt <<'EOF'
Merge origin/main (0.26.5) into feat/streams-csv-signatures

32 upstream commits, mostly the mysqli-over-PDO bridge, the 0.26.5 release, and a sweep adding
intent comments to the runtime emitters. Four conflicts, each resolved by deciding what is TRUE
rather than by picking a side.

`stream_wrapper_register` — OURS, and this one had to be looked at rather than taken. Upstream
validates the scheme alphabet and refuses a duplicate, which this branch also does; but upstream
still scans `_user_wrappers`, the fixed 64-slot static array, where this branch reserves from a
heap-backed table that grows on demand — php imposes no limit, and the old array silently refused
the 65th registration. Taking `theirs` would have reverted that. This branch's version is a
superset: same alphabet check, same duplicate refusal, plus the refusal to shadow a BUILT-IN scheme
(`stream_wrapper_register("file", …)` is false in php, and upstream's version accepts it) and the
unbounded table.

That comparison also turned up something worth recording: the scheme validation exists in the MERGE
BASE, which is an ancestor of this branch, and did NOT exist on this branch. No commit removed it —
`git log -S` shows only the commit that ADDED it, because a merge that discards one side's hunks
never registers as a change to the file. An earlier merge dropped it silently. It was found by
MEASURING (`x_y` and `x y` registered as schemes, which php refuses) and rewritten, before the
history was consulted at all.

So the loss was swept for rather than assumed unique: comparing the runtime SYMBOL SETS between the
base and this branch gives 783 → 931 global entry points with exactly ONE missing, `__rt_sscanf`,
removed deliberately when scanf moved from 700 lines of assembly per arch to a PHP prelude. At the
level of all labels, 149 are missing across 18 files; the large ones are rewrites this branch made
on purpose (sscanf 39, fgetcsv 19, stream_filter 16, fputcsv 15), and the behaviour sweep measures
those families conformant against `php -n` 8.5.6.

`CHANGELOG.md` — UNION. Both sides added entries under `[Unreleased]`; choosing one would drop the
other's release notes silently.

`docs/php/streams.md` — MEASURED, because each side had half of it right. This branch documented
the full parameter list but a bare `array` return and claimed `$escape` defaults to `''`; upstream
documented `array|false` and the `while (($row = fgetcsv($h)) !== false)` loop but abbreviated the
parameters. php 8.5.6 reports `fgetcsv(mixed $stream, ?int $length = null, string $separator = ',',
string $enclosure = '"', string $escape = '\\'): array|false` — so the default is a BACKSLASH, this
branch's doc was wrong about it, and the catalogue (`DefaultSpec::Str("\\")`) was right, which is
how the contradiction surfaced. The resolved line carries the measured signature.

`docs/php/system-and-io.md` — per LINE. `file_get_contents()` and `file()` keep this branch's
wording, which describes the stream context this branch actually publishes; upstream's "the
stream-context parameter is not supported" is stale. Upstream's more precise `json_encode()`
wording (lowercase-hex `\uXXXX` versus the uppercase-hex `JSON_HEX_*` replacements) and its new
paragraph on `url_stat()` dispatch are kept.

Verified on the merged tree: `cargo test -p elephc --lib` 1 528 passed, `codegen_tests io::` 1 024
passed.
EOF
